title: DNA/RNA Extraction and qPCR for Bacterial Abundance in Halichondria panicea
author: Lara Schmittmann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bxwwppfe
materials: Extract DNA from samples fixed in RNAlater (stored at -80°C) or flash frozen (stored at -80°C) Qiagen PowerSoil Kit Input: 70-200 mg tissue Process max.24 samples at a time, depending on experience

Extract DNA from bacterial recolonization pellets flash frozen (stored at -80°C) Qiagen Blood+Tissue kit Input: cell pellet Process max.24 samples at a time, depending on experience No good results were achieved with the Qiagen PowerSoil Kit for cell pellets.

steps.title: Prepare work area and reagents
steps.instruction: Clean all surfaces and instruments with ethanol then RNase‑Away; work under a fume‑hood wearing nitrile gloves; prepare fresh β‑mercaptoethanol stock for each extraction (6 µl β‑mercaptoethanol + 594 µl RLT buffer); limit processing to 6–12 samples per batch.

steps.title: Thaw and label tissue
steps.instruction: Thaw sponge tissue samples on ice; label the side of each 2 ml lysis tube (labels on the lid may disappear during PowerLyzer step). Keep remaining samples on ice.

steps.title: Cut tissue and weigh
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps and a sterile petri dish, cut each sample into pieces and weigh approximately 80 mg into the labeled lysis tube; use a new petri dish and scalpel for each sample to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Lyse tissue with β‑ME/RLT
steps.instruction: Add 600 µl β‑mercaptoethanol/RLT buffer to the tube under the hood; homogenize in a PowerLyzer at 3000 rpm for 30 seconds; keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 minutes; carefully transfer the supernatant to a new 2 ml collection tube without disturbing the pellet; work at room temperature from this point onward.

steps.title: Add ethanol and mix
steps.instruction: Add one volume (~370 µl) of 70 % molecular‑grade ethanol to the supernatant; mix thoroughly by pipetting; proceed immediately to column binding.

steps.title: Bind RNA to RNeasy column
steps.instruction: Transfer up to 700 µl (including any precipitate) to an RNeasy spin column placed in a 2 ml collection tube; centrifuge 30 seconds at 10 000 rpm; discard flow‑through; reuse the collection tube; repeat if the volume exceeds 700 µl.

steps.title: Wash column with RW1
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl RW1 buffer to the spin column; centrifuge 30 seconds at 10 000 rpm; discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash column with RPE (first)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl RPE buffer; centrifuge 30 seconds at 10 000 rpm; discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash column with RPE (second)
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µl RPE buffer; centrifuge 2 minutes at 10 000 rpm; place the spin column in a fresh 2 ml collection tube and centrifuge 1 minute at maximum speed to remove residual buffer.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the spin column to a fresh 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube; add 60 µl EB buffer directly onto the membrane; incubate 10 minutes at room temperature; centrifuge 1 minute at 10 000 rpm; keep eluate on ice.

steps.title: DNase treatment of RNA
steps.instruction: Under a clean bench, add 3 µl SUPERase‑IN (0.05 × RNA volume) to the 60 µl RNA and mix gently; add 6 µl 10× DNase I buffer (0.1 × RNA) and 1.2 µl DNase (DNA‑free™ DNA Removal Kit) and mix gently; incubate 20 minutes at 37 °C with occasional mixing; add 6 µl DNase I inactivation reagent, mix well, and incubate 2–5 minutes at room temperature, vortexing briefly each minute; centrifuge 1.5 minutes at 10 300 rpm and transfer the clear supernatant (RNA) to a new tube, avoiding the white inactivation reagent.

steps.title: Aliquot and freeze RNA
steps.instruction: Immediately take a 5 µl aliquot for quality/quantity checks (Nanodrop, Qubit, PCR) and a 2 µl aliquot for capillary electrophoresis; freeze all aliquots at –80 °C; split the remaining RNA into two equal parts so one can stay frozen for downstream transcriptomics.

steps.title: cDNA synthesis
steps.instruction: Use the iScript kit following the manufacturer’s guidelines; thaw reverse transcriptase only immediately before adding to the master mix and keep on ice; use 500 ng RNA per 20 µl reaction with random primers.

steps.title: Store and dilute cDNA
steps.instruction: Store cDNA dilutions at –20 °C; dilute each cDNA 1:5 with TE buffer for use in qPCR.

steps.title: Prepare primer stocks
steps.instruction: Dilute each primer pair to 50 µM in TE buffer; aliquot 10 µl portions and freeze at –20 °C; use each aliquot only once; work under a clean bench with sterile equipment to avoid contamination, especially for eubacterial 16S primers.

steps.title: Prepare standard curves
steps.instruction: Prepare one DNA and one cDNA standard curve; make larger volumes to reuse across experiments; measure the highest‑concentration standard with the Qubit high‑sensitivity kit, calculate copy numbers (see http://cels.uri.edu/gsc/cndna.html), and create serial dilutions (e.g., 1:10 by adding 200 µl PCR product + 1800 µl tRNA water; optional 1:5 by 400 µl + 1600 µl).

steps.title: Measure and dilute DNA extracts
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration of all extracts with Qubit; dilute each extract to 6 ng/µl with DNase/RNase‑free water so that 5 µl template provides 30 ng per qPCR reaction.

steps.title: Set up qPCR plate
steps.instruction: Include standard curves for each primer set on every 96‑well plate; run both total‑bacterial 16S and Halichondribacter‑specific primers on the same plate; add negative controls (qPCR mix + water). Prepare master mix per primer pair: 0.16 µl forward primer (50 µM), 0.16 µl reverse primer (50 µM), 10 µl 2× qPCR mix, 4.68 µl H₂O (total 20 µl per reaction). Pipette 15 µl master mix into each well, then add 5 µl template (gDNA: 30 ng, cDNA: 1:5 dilution of 500 ng RNA); use a new tip for each well; seal with optical adhesive foil and briefly spin down.

steps.title: Run qPCR
steps.instruction: Run on the appropriate instrument with the following program: 96 °C 2 min; 94 °C 30 s; 40 cycles of 60 °C 30 s (plate read); 72 °C 1 min (plate read); melt curve from 60 °C to 90 °C in 0.5 °C increments, 5 s per step. Run the plate immediately or store at 4 °C in the dark and run within 24 h.

steps.title: Validate qPCR products
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1% agarose gel with nucleic‑acid stain (e.g., GelGreen) using large wells for 50 µl per well; load selected PCR products, run electrophoresis, visualize bands under blue light, cut out the correct band with a sterile scalpel, clean up using the Macherey‑Nagel NucleoSpin kit, and pool if needed; run a subset of qPCR products on a gel each experiment to confirm a single band of expected size.

steps.title: Check melt curves
steps.instruction: Examine melt curves for each primer set; ensure a single peak and that melt‑curve profiles of standards overlap those of experimental samples.

steps.title: DNA extraction for standards (optional)
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s protocol for PowerBeadTubes and PowerLyzer (3500 rpm, 2 × 30 s bead beating with 45 s pause). After extraction, take a 5 µl aliquot for quality/quantity assessment (Nanodrop, Qubit, PCR). Store DNA at –20 °C for short‑term or –80 °C for long‑term storage.
